preservation, loss, inverse, invalidation or other relation semantics

concepts.label: TypedRelation record

language and how its result is judged. A predicate that is not
deterministically decidable states the required probabilistic or human
judgment kind rather than pretending to be a machine proof

concepts.label: Constraint record

concepts.definition: Latitude is an explicit permission set inside a constraint boundary, with fields id, applies_to, allowed_variation, forbidden_variation, context, owner, scope, basis and invalidation. grounding.quote:
Silence is not latitude. Latitude grants no authority beyond its owner,
scope, basis and invalidation law

concepts.label: Latitude record

concepts.definition: Residual is first-class model uncertainty with fields id, subject, kind, uncertainty, consequence, context, owner, scope, basis, re_entry and invalidation. kind resolves a declared ResidualKind whose signature defines lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation domains; undeclared kinds or values refuse structural admission.

`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines
its lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry and invalidation
domains. An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission
(P3).

concepts.label: Residual record

concepts.definition: The source's core result domain contains satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis. Constraint judgments and operation outcomes answer different named predicates. Missing assessments have no closed result. Operation stops include hold, gap, refusal(constraint) and refusal(basis), with cause-sensitive mappings rather than a generic success/failure collapse.

grounding.quote:
| holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
| failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
| indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
| out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
| invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |

concepts.label: Core results and operation stops

`gap` or `refusal(basis)` (AC-007). `Boundary_Z` records excluded,
external, unresolved, translated and invalidation-sensitive seams. A
projection is not a new semantic owner.

concepts.label: Model projection

families of a basis model. It does not mutate the basis. Override,
disambiguation, equivalence, specialisation or translation exists only as
a typed relation with exact authority, direction, scope, basis,
preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation semantics

subject. Promotion is an explicit relation between the unchanged subject

concepts.label: Judgment record

binding under that owner's authority

concepts.label: Traversal contract

concepts.definition: The subject's F_D, F_P and F_H have identities urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d, :f-p and :f-h. F_D classifies deterministic evaluation/proof returning a judgment without doing the judged domain construction. F_P classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or proposal without inherent semantic, admission, acceptance or closure authority. F_H classifies explicit human adjudication under exact identity, grant, subject, basis and decision contract; human presence grants no ambient authority.

grounding.quote:
- `F_D` classifies deterministic evaluation or proof over declared
  properties. It returns a judgment and does not perform the domain
  construction being judged (P6).
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance or closure authority merely because it is useful
  or repeatable (P6, P0; instance premise (iii) of §1 Foundation to law).
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis and decision contract. Human presence
  grants no ambient authority (P6).

applicable semantic acceptance judgment. The interpretation contract is

signature.

A constraint surface states, for a declared subject and work boundary,
the obligations and the permitted freedom of the work: its objects and
their meanings, the predicates and dependencies that bear on it, the
admissible operations, the required results, the authority, the evidence
and the conditions still unresolved. It constrains the work without
prescribing the worker's internal solution strategy beyond those
obligations

specified expected distinction, and its status. A status names what
exists: a fixture designed, runs by a fresh constructor, or an assessment

of what exists, not a result. A run is not a pass; only an assessment
records one.

exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor cites the accepted relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta instead of recreating evidence.

When the
design's co-evolution condition holds, the two chains may proceed together
without making implementation semantic authority; design still owns the
structural HOW. Where the design is not decision-complete, the relation is
design-gated at the smallest causally closed affected decision set and
retained implementation follows its acceptance. An unchanged
`realization_refactor` (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes) cites the accepted
relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not
recreate the evidence

constraints.statement: Semantic derivation supplies expected-result assertion provenance; feedback supplies execution provenance and cannot select or accept the affected semantic answer. Agreement can share an error; disagreement requires diagnosis. Co-evolution is permitted only under the design's condition and confers no implementation semantic authority. Design owns structural HOW; an incomplete design gates retained implementation on acceptance of the smallest causally closed affected decision set.

continuation. The design profile supplies the governing-frame,
transformation-admission, invariant-reconstruction,
computational-realisation and module evidence that relation consumes; it
does not define a second execution protocol

The profile supplies governing-frame, transformation-admission, invariant-reconstruction, computational-realisation and module evidence consumed by that relation, without defining another execution protocol.

grounding.quote:
- the final implementation is traceable to the accepted ontology;
- the final implementation is traceable to design and module boundary

- unit tests are traceable to module ownership, not only to helper
  layout;
- implementation-first discoveries are reconciled into the ontology and

constraints.statement: Final implementation traces to accepted ontology and design/module-boundary assets; unit tests trace to module ownership, not only helper layout. Implementation-first discoveries must be reconciled into ontology and domain/sequence/state evidence before promotion or closure. Hidden controllers or alternative authority paths cannot compensate for unrealised declared constructors. Closure proof is re-expressed against module ownership even when tests were discovered from implementation. The module boundary enables a common ownership audit but outranks neither constitutional truth nor ratified design; jumping from design/code to tests without reconstructing it is too weak.

conditions: A complete evidence chain is claimed.
exceptions: Where a reference realisation exists, use the reference-realisation chain described in the statement.
constraints.statement: The minimum chain is constitutional WHAT → accepted ontology → target design → target module-boundary assets and ontology-derived carrier inventory → accepted domain/sequence/state projections with axiom evaluation → implementation → unit tests derived from the same ontology and module boundary. With a reference realisation, the seven stages instead are constitutional WHAT → reference design → accepted target ontology plus reference-to-ontology mapping → target design mapping → target module-boundary assets plus ontology-derived carriers → accepted domain/sequence/state projections with axiom evaluation → implementation and unit tests derived from the same ontology.

conditions: Unit tests are under the design profile.
exceptions: Helper-level tests are permitted, but cannot become the canonical module-boundary proof surface.
constraints.statement: A unit test should trace to accepted ontology and applicable entity/lifecycle/authority/function/effect/projection law, governing module design, declared active or equivalent carrier inventory, module-bounded domain/sequence/state projections, and owned requirement families. This is a recommendation, distinct from required module ownership. Tests are not primarily authored from helper boundaries, private-method layout, incidental branches, temporary decomposition or mock convenience hiding the contract. The required question is what the module owns and what proof that ownership requires.

grounding.quote:
Canonical rule (P6): module-owned unit tests are authoritative for module
proof; broader integration, scenario and sandbox lanes remain downstream
proof families; transitional slice-gating tests may exist, but they do not
replace module-derived unit proof. If a module has code but no
module-derived unit test lane, the module is not closure-ready under the
design profile. What such a lane claims, and what it never closes, is
the unit frame of §7.

constraints.statement: Module-owned tests are authoritative for module proof; integration, scenario and sandbox lanes remain downstream. Transitional slice-gating tests may exist but cannot replace module-derived proof. A module with code and no module-derived unit lane is not closure-ready. Realisation-authority ownership does not extend to Product UAT or acceptance meaning.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed claims and non-closure boundaries of ASSURANCE §7's unit frame are not supplied.

conditions: For each governed boundary.
constraints.statement: Before design-method closure, design evidence states or points to statements of all nine lifecycle items: upstream intent/requirement authority; build/realisation; assurance/proof; release/packaging; deployment/install; live use/invocation; observed telemetry/projection/monitoring; retirement/revocation/supersession/decommission; and lifecycle-decision owner, source truth and authority boundary.

conditions: For every lifecycle phase in design evidence.

grounding.quote:
Each lifecycle phase takes one of the three answers that
[SPEC_METHOD §2 Operational lifecycle sufficiency](SPEC_METHOD.md#operational-lifecycle-sufficiency)
owns, applied here to design evidence: answered by the active design,
requirement, release, deployment or telemetry surface; declared not
applicable with a reason; or recorded as a named `Gap:` or `Unanswered:`
item, which in design evidence also names its owning follow-up.

constraints.statement: Each phase is answered by an active design, requirement, release, deployment or telemetry surface; declared not applicable with a reason; or recorded as a named Gap: or Unanswered: with an owning follow-up. These are declared evidence states, not result values. A bare phase list is not design-method evidence. A named gap remains a residual until its owning follow-up disposes it.
constraints.uncertainty: The canonical phase chain is referenced but not reproduced.

exceptions: A module may proceed with exposed missing release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement truth only when the gap is explicitly governed.

grounding.quote:
Implementation proves the selected lifecycle path only within the
authority it owns. Code, tests, generated artifacts or runtime fixtures may
confirm that a lifecycle claim is real, but they may not invent lifecycle
authority that the product, requirements, design, release or operational
surface did not declare (P6). If the checklist exposes missing release,
deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement truth, the module may still
proceed only when that gap is explicitly governed; it may not close by
relying on local convention, implementation precedent, mutable runtime
state, prompt prose or test-only fixture behaviour

constraints.statement: Implementation proves the selected path only within its owned authority. Code, tests, generated artifacts and runtime fixtures may confirm claims but cannot invent undeclared product, requirements, design, release or operational authority. Closure cannot rely on local convention, implementation precedent, mutable runtime state, prompt prose or test-only fixture behaviour.

The predecessor's "must"
is written in the indicative; "should", "may" and "minimum" keep their
force.
superseded in its scenario-writing and scenario-failure sentences, proposed and pending the product owner's acceptance

Generalisations keep profile terms out of tier 2: Ontology→ontology; IACS→declared carriers; three-view evidence→domain/sequence/state evidence; co_evolution_admissible(B)/decision_complete(B)→design conditions; graph function/GTL module→published profile function/module; this method→design profile; execution relation→ACTIVATION §1; RELEASE_METHOD→RELEASE. These references establish provenance. The definitions and laws of this
member are the sole normative authority for the meaning of `a_c` within
the selected complete cut. A consumer needs no implicit representation of
the method, no particular carrier and no downstream implementation to
interpret the calculus

F_D/F_P/F_H are generic identities introduced here, not imports from equal-spelled runtime/profile/realisation/application shorthand. Nominal equality creates no identity, import or equivalence. Exact basis issuance resolves the derivation routes into absolute predecessor-cut principle_refs. Models, encodings, tools and successful applications cannot amend principles or calculus.
constraints.uncertainty: This describes the subject's authority claim and does not install it as the interpretation workflow's authority.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

§11 records where each predecessor claim is carried and decides nothing.
The table is new in this corpus. Purpose and material relation: an actor
started on this member sees which rules of the calculus follow from the

choice is presented as derived

exceptions: An additional fundamental family requires an explicit compatible calculus extension; empty populations are allowed only when the selected signature requires no member of that kind.

grounding.quote:
`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population
is finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and
record identities are unique across their disjoint union. Let `Local_M` be
that union. Then `I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M`, where every
member of `External_M` is admitted only through one signature-declared
external reference domain and exact resolution relation.

constraints.statement: Every signature imports core identities unchanged and may specialise fields/value/reference domains and admissible kinds, not remove, rename, shadow or silently add core families. An extra subject sort cannot create a fundamental family. Unknown kinds/fields require a new signature or explicit compatible extension. Signatures define every field/value domain, reference cardinality/domain, relation endpoint sorts, constraint subject/predicate domains, residual subject/uncertainty/consequence/re-entry domains, judgment input/output/evidence/stops and permitted traversal functor kinds. Population_M is total and finite with globally unique, disjoint record membership; hidden records, extra families, duplicate population identities or identities without one lawful local/external resolution refuse the model.

conditions: Every scalar or collection member carrying an identity reference.

grounding.quote:
Every scalar or collection member that carries an identity reference is
checked through that function. A local reference resolves across the exact
`Population_M` family named by its target record kind; a reference to a
semantic object also satisfies the declared target sort. An external
reference resolves through exactly one declared external target kind and
basis relation. No reference may resolve both locally and externally.
Missing field domains, wrong-family targets, wrong-sort targets, ambiguous
targets and dangling external identities refuse structural admission

constraints.statement: RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind, field) declares cardinality, allowed local record kinds, allowed semantic-object sorts, allowed external target kinds and required basis relation. Each identity-bearing scalar/member is checked against it. Local resolution uses the exact population and applicable sort; external resolution uses exactly one declared target kind and basis relation; local/external dual resolution is prohibited. Missing domains, wrong families/sorts, ambiguity and dangling external identities refuse structural admission.

exceptions: A subject model may independently represent the concept of a record kind, without satisfying its core population requirement.

grounding.quote:
A traversal, transformation or
judgment is not placed in `O` merely by reifying its name as a semantic
object. A subject model may independently represent the concept of a
record kind, but that representation does not satisfy the core population
law

constraints.statement: SemanticObject, TypedRelation, Constraint, Latitude and Residual populate O/E/C/L/X; traversal, transformation and judgment records populate V/T/J. Reifying their names as semantic objects does not substitute for the operational record populations.

grounding.quote:
The objects these laws govern are the records of §2, §3 and §5 and the
ontology of FOUNDATIONS §2; where a law names identity, authority, basis
or residual, the definition is FOUNDATIONS' and the law is this member's.

constraints.statement: The laws govern §2/§3/§5 records and FOUNDATIONS §2 ontology. Identity, authority, basis and residual definitions remain with FOUNDATIONS; the calculus member owns its laws over them.
constraints.uncertainty: FOUNDATIONS definitions are referenced, not supplied in full.

conditions: Any admitted object, relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal, transformation specialisation or judgment.

grounding.quote:
Every admitted object, relation, constraint, latitude, residual,
traversal, transformation specialisation and judgment belongs to one
declared signature. Every fundamental record also occurs exactly once in
the total `Population_M` function under its declared `RecordKind_ac`.
Missing, duplicate, shadowed or unknown record kinds and populations fail
closed

constraints.statement: Every admitted record belongs to one declared signature and occurs exactly once in total Population_M under its declared core kind. Missing, duplicate, shadowed or unknown kinds/populations fail closed.

conditions: Every identity in I.

grounding.quote:
So an identity resolves one member under one type,
context, owner, scope and basis. That equal representations do not
establish equal meaning is FOUNDATIONS §2, Representation. The `a_c`
binding beside it: equal spelling, payload equality, position in any
structure and carrier equality do not establish semantic identity

constraints.statement: Identity resolves one member under one type, context, owner, scope and basis. Owner maps to authority, type to kind, and resolved member to denoted value; context/scope/basis are required additional coordinates. Equal spelling, payload, structural position or carrier does not establish semantic identity.

conditions: Every referenced identity.

grounding.quote:
Every referenced identity resolves exactly once in the applicable model or
through one explicit external relation. Resolution uses the exact
`RefDomain_Sigma(source_record_kind, field)` declaration across the
model's record populations. Dangling, duplicate, wrong-record-kind,
wrong-sort, wrong-basis, locally-and-externally ambiguous or
undeclared-field references refuse structural admission

constraints.statement: Every reference resolves exactly once locally or through one explicit external relation using its exact RefDomain_Sigma declaration. Dangling, duplicate, wrong-kind, wrong-sort, wrong-basis, local/external ambiguity and undeclared-field references refuse structural admission. Refusal's core value follows AC-007's cause rules, including basis-only classification for wrong-basis mismatches.

exceptions: Direction is not material when the relation kind explicitly declares symmetry.

grounding.quote:
A relation is lawful only when its kind admits the exact source and target
sorts and all required qualifiers are present. Direction is material
unless the relation kind explicitly declares symmetry

constraints.statement: Lawful relations require kind-admitted exact endpoint sorts and every required qualifier; direction is material unless expressly symmetric.

conditions: Objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals, transformations, projections and judgments.

grounding.quote:
Objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals,
transformations, projections and judgments retain their declared semantic,
operation, evaluation and decision authority

constraints.statement: All listed records/operations retain declared semantic, operation, evaluation and decision authority. Copying, interpreting, encoding, evaluating or transporting a record transfers none.

exceptions: Mixed bases require an explicitly owned composite-basis relation.

grounding.quote:
This law binds the same rule to every fundamental record and model
of `a_c`: each binds an exact basis, the composite-basis relation of a
mixed basis is an explicitly owned record, and individually valid
coordinates do not create a coherent composite basis by proximity

constraints.statement: Every result, fundamental record and model binds its exact basis. Individually valid coordinates do not establish coherent composite basis by proximity.

conditions: A constraint judgment is performed.

grounding.quote:
A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result

constraints.statement: For 'the constraint predicate holds for its governed subject on the exact basis', holds→satisfied; failed→falsified with named counterexample; undecidable admissible evidence→indeterminate with deciding evidence named; outside applies_to/context/scope→out_of_frame with the needed undeclared relation and its source-given owner named; unsupported subject/basis→invalid_basis with repair named. A declared refinement maps each value to exactly one core value without raising standing. Failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope and invalid-basis states never coerce to satisfied. A nonperformed judgment has no closed result, is not indeterminate, and remains planned without result in conjunctions.

conditions: Closure, projection, structural admission, transformation application or interpretation is applied.

grounding.quote: | `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |

constraints.statement: For 'the operation yields its declared result on the exact basis', returned declared result→satisfied, establishing only availability of a proposed model/successor, never acceptance/admission. hold→indeterminate when needed evidence/observation/disposition is unadmitted, with deciding acquisition in a residual. gap→invalid_basis only while a needed member/reference/resolution/declaration remains undecided by its declared resolution relation. An evaluated reference yielding no target is dangling and refuses, as does a local reference with no record. Refusal names its condition, admits no record/model/carrier and silently drops nothing. An unapplied operation has no outcome; a stop gap is a closed invalid_basis result, distinct from a conjunction's missing-result gap.

conditions: An operation returns refusal.
exceptions: A basis mismatch, including a wrong-basis reference or relation qualifier coordinate, is always a basis condition and never a signature-constraint violation.

grounding.quote:
It is
a condition of the basis, in the structural admission that judges that
model or record as in every other operation, and never a violated
constraint of a signature, even where the signature declares the basis
relation; a refusal that names only such a mismatch is `refusal(basis)`.

A demonstrated violation takes priority even alongside a basis condition: retain its falsified counterexample and separately report the basis condition as invalid_basis for the unsupported evaluation's own predicate, with repair. A violation in an input used as basis is a basis condition for that operation. Thus AC-001 violation is constraint refusal when admitting the model, but basis refusal when projecting over it. Every refined refusal has one core value.

grounding.quote:
Two values may differ lawfully only through an applicable latitude record
or transformation relation. An implementation preference, a probabilistic
choice or a human presence is not implicit latitude.

constraints.statement: Lawful difference requires applicable latitude or a transformation relation. Implementation preference, probabilistic choice and human presence confer no implicit latitude.

exceptions: An authorised disposition creates an exact successor model.

Every material uncertainty, omission, translation loss, unresolved
boundary or unproven relation remains in `X` until an authorised
disposition creates an exact successor model. Absence from a projection is
not resolution

Projection, compression, interpretation or encoding cannot erase a
residual. It remains represented, is explicitly dispositioned by competent
authority, or causes refusal

constraints.statement: Material unresolved content remains in X until authorised disposition creates an exact successor. Projection, compression, interpretation and encoding cannot erase it; it remains represented, is competently dispositioned or causes refusal. Omission from a projection is not resolution.

The result is defined only when `Z`, `R`, required-edge semantics, basis
and scope are exact and the fixed point is finite and unique. Failure to
establish those conditions returns a gap or refusal: `gap` where a
condition is unresolved on the basis, otherwise `refusal(basis)`, because
each condition bears on the basis the closure acts on (AC-007).

Failure returns gap for unresolved basis conditions, otherwise refusal(basis); both map to invalid_basis. ACTIVATION §2 applies closure to context construction under an envelope.

grounding.quote:
It is a reference, so the rule
that no reference trims a required member to fit a carrier or budget,
stated at [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Reference versus
body, applies to it: here the required members are those of the material
closure of `Z`, and a capability budget is one such budget.

Required members cannot be trimmed for carrier, budget or capability fit. Its gap/refusal comes from contained closure or input model and is gap or refusal(basis). grounding.quote:
`domain_model` and `codomain_model` resolve exact content identities of
the complete input and proposed successor models. Each model identity
commits to its exact calculus basis, signature identity, complete finite
`Population_M`, complete `External_M`, exact external-resolution map and
selected model-content identity under the owning identity law. A mutable
locator, a model-family name, a partial projection or a population digest
without the exact model identity refuses

Domain/codomain identify complete exact models committing basis, signature, full populations, externals, resolution map and content identity; mutable locators, family names, partial views or population digests alone refuse. grounding.quote:
Every removed identity is absent from the successor. Every introduced
identity is absent from the input and carries a complete lawful record in
exactly one successor population. Every input local-record identity is
classified exactly once as preserved or removed; no local record may be
silently dropped, retained or duplicated

Changed fields/basis/kind, nominally equal IDs, equivalence or unbound preservation claims refuse preservation. Equivalence may relate removed and introduced identities but cannot preserve one identity. Every input record is classified exactly once; introduced records are complete, lawful, novel and in one successor population.

conditions: External references occur in a transformation's domain or codomain.

grounding.quote:
`Resolution_M` is a model coordinate supplied by the signature-declared
external reference relation, not a ninth fundamental record family. Every
field is identity-bearing and exact. One external identity has exactly one
resolution tuple in one model; a missing, ambiguous or extra tuple refuses

constraints.statement: Each external identity has exactly one exact Resolution_M tuple: external_identity, reference_domain, external_target_kind, resolved_target_identity, basis_relation, resolution_basis, evidence_identity. It is a model coordinate, not a ninth record family; missing/ambiguous/extra tuples refuse. External accounting proves E_b = EP_t disjoint_union ER_t; E_b_prime = EP_t disjoint_union EN_t; EN_t intersect E_b = empty; ER_t intersect E_b_prime = empty. Each preserved resolution has exactly one witness naming resolution, both models, both resolution tuples, decision equal and evidence; witnesses cover exactly EP_t. conditions: Transformation application.
exceptions: Material residuals may leave the successor only with an exact authorised disposition in transformation evidence.

grounding.quote:
The exact transformation identity `t` declares every mutation it may
perform. The input model remains unchanged; `M_b_prime*` is a proposed
successor. A proposed successor does not accept or admit itself (P6). The
stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` take their core values under AC-007 by
their causes.

constraints.statement: The exact transformation declares every permitted mutation; input remains unchanged and output is only a proposed successor, never self-admitted or self-accepted. Material residuals persist absent exact authorised disposition. Failure to establish any model identity, basis, population, local/external partition, equality, resolution witness, residual or codomain equation refuses. Stops use AC-007 cause mappings. FOUNDATIONS consumes the law as conservation accounting, not as an executed step here.

exceptions: A different parent core value requires a different parent value declared by its owning member.

grounding.quote:
Each refined value, whether the stop contract or a
`stop_states` declares it, names its parent value and its cause and maps
to its parent's core value: a value refined from `hold` to indeterminate,
from `gap` or `refusal(basis)` to invalid_basis, and from
`refusal(constraint)` to falsified. No refined value takes `satisfied`.

constraints.statement: Omega_v adds no core value; each stop maps to exactly one nonsatisfied core value. Signature stop contracts declare additional stops and may refine by cause; traversal stop_states binds its mapping and may refine further. Each refinement names parent and cause and retains the parent's core value, never raises standing. Actor, executor, domain operation and functor kind are distinct; Encode/Interpret/Serialize/Measure are not kind aliases. Sharing a kind shares no traversal identity, semantics, inputs, outputs, authority or evidence. 'Functor kind' alone makes no categorical claim; claimed categorical laws require the specified formal demonstration.
constraints.uncertainty: The external formal-fragment demonstration requirements are not supplied.

conditions: Every functor application.

grounding.quote:
Every functor application binds exactly one functor kind and one traversal
identity. Applying any `F_*` kind without the bracketed traversal identity
`[v]` is incomplete (P3; rc.2 #ac-015-functor-classification). Such an
application violates this law, and its outcome is `refusal(constraint)`
under AC-007; this sense of incomplete is not the construction-availability
value `incomplete` of a step

constraints.statement: An application binds exactly one functor kind and traversal identity. Omitting [v] is a violation yielding refusal(constraint), hence falsified, not the construction-availability value incomplete of an ACTIVATION step.

conditions: Two traversals are composed.

grounding.quote:
Composition retains both traversal identities, intermediate results,
judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stop states. It cannot
flatten probabilistic proposal, deterministic evaluation and human
decision into one undifferentiated operation. `a_c` prescribes no
universal `F_P -> F_D -> F_H` sequence; each application owns its lawful
topology

constraints.statement: Composition is lawful only when the first result type and judgment satisfy the next exact domain/preconditions. It preserves both identities and all intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stops. Proposal, evaluation and human decision cannot be flattened; no universal F_P→F_D→F_H sequence is prescribed, and each application owns its lawful topology.

grounding.quote:
The proposed model `M_subject*` does not become accepted through
construction. Structural evaluation can prove closed shape, reference
typing, identity derivation and basis coherence. It cannot prove that
probabilistic semantic selection retained every material subject meaning.
Semantic acceptance remains a separately recorded authority judgment

constraints.statement: Constructing a model does not accept it. Structural evaluation can establish shape, reference typing, identity derivation and basis coherence but cannot establish retention of every material meaning by probabilistic selection. Semantic acceptance is a separate recorded authority judgment; interpretation stops map by cause under AC-007.

conditions: Every admitted record and every evaluated subject declaration.
exceptions: Model-local content is allowed when explicitly identified under competent authority.

grounding.quote:
Every admitted model record maps to exact subject provenance or is
explicitly identified as model-local content under competent authority.
Every evaluated subject declaration has a retained, omitted, residual,
inapplicable or refused disposition. Interpretation cannot treat absence
as immateriality without a recorded basis and authority

constraints.statement: Each admitted record maps to exact provenance or explicitly authorised model-local content. Each evaluated declaration has retained, omitted, residual, inapplicable or refused disposition. Absence cannot be treated as immateriality without recorded basis and authority.

grounding.quote:
the
structural conformance of a model covers its closed syntax, types,
identities, references, bases and mechanically decidable predicates, and
the semantic fidelity of an interpretation covers its meaning and
materiality

constraints.statement: Structural conformance concerns closed syntax, types, identities, references, bases and mechanically decidable predicates; semantic fidelity concerns meaning and materiality. Structural success is evidence for semantic review, never its substitute. EVALUATION §2 owns the general separation; AC-018 binds it to a_c.

conditions: A model claims M_b satisfies a_c[Sigma].
exceptions: A checker may claim semantic or authority decisions only under an exact lawful model-supplied decision contract.

grounding.quote:
A checker may decide the structural subset. No generic checker may claim
the semantic or authority subset unless the model supplies an exact lawful
decision contract for it

constraints.statement: Validity requires resolving signature/exact calculus basis; every record satisfying AC-001–AC-009; each claimed closure, projection, overlay, transformation, judgment and composition satisfying its applicable law; fidelity/residual dispositions binding exact subject; distinct structural evaluation and semantic acceptance, both required where claimed; and resolving every evidence, provenance, invalidation and re-entry coordinate. Checkers may decide the structural subset without thereby deciding semantic or authority subsets.

conditions: Encoding or admitted-encoding evidence is claimed.

grounding.quote:
Encoding requires `J_X.decision = accepted` and exact equality between the
judgment subject identity and digest and `M_X`; hold or refusal cannot be
encoded.

constraints.statement: Encode_C(M_X,J_X) requires accepted J_X over the unchanged model with exact identity/digest equality; hold or refusal cannot be encoded. Carrier admission uses F_D[v_carrier_admission](G_C,Profile_C,CarrierBasis_C) and judges unchanged bytes. Neither judgment enters its subject identity; admitted evidence is exactly (G_C,J_X,D_C). Accepted/admitted each map to satisfied for their own predicate; hold/refuse map by AC-007 cause and never count as acceptance.

exceptions: An external selecting/releasing authority can grant Product status to a layer.

grounding.quote:
An encoding failure does not change `a_c.X`. An interpretation failure
does not change `a_c`. A downstream success cannot ratify an upstream
layer or basis. None of these layers is automatically an independently
released Product. The external authority that selects and releases one
owns that Product status.

constraints.statement: Each layer has independent content identity, judgments, supersession and proof obligations. Calculus qualification evaluates internal coherence against the full declared law set; interpretation proves exact-subject fidelity; encoding proves faithful canonical encoding of an accepted model. Encoding failure does not alter its model, interpretation failure does not alter calculus, and downstream success ratifies no upstream layer/basis. Product release is not automatic; SPEC_METHOD §6 applies this separation to lineage.

conditions: An exact released edition identity is issued.

grounding.quote:
The record uses RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes. Duplicate
object names are rejected before canonicalisation.
`derivation_basis.principle_refs` is duplicate-free and sorted by
ascending unsigned UTF-16 code units.

constraints.statement: Release URIs are absolute and immutable; principle_refs is a nonempty absolute semantic-address URI array; digests use sha256: plus 64 lowercase hex characters. Reject duplicate object names before RFC 8785 JCS; deduplicate and sort principle_refs by ascending unsigned UTF-16 units. Identity is urn:stdo:axiomatic-calculus-basis:sha256: plus sha256(JCS(record)). Derivation binds one exact accepted predecessor cut and the complete finite clause set identified by the derivation account, resolved inside that cut without hard-coded count and recomputed when the account changes; it cannot depend on publication carrier or the identity being created. Publication binds a distinct immutable successor and exact member bytes, with member URI inside release URI. Same-release calculus citations are publication/cross-context, not derivation, relations.

grounding.quote:
The owning Product defines the canonical record grammar and issuance
authority for those downstream identities. It cannot omit the upstream
identities or replace them with mutable locators

constraints.statement: id(a_c.X) binds at least exact calculus ID, subject-basis ID, interpretation contract, selected model-content identity and semantic-selection ledger identity/digest. External accepted J_X points to unchanged identity/digest; accepted interpretation is (a_c.X,J_X), with no cyclic embedding. id(a_c.X.C) binds at least exact interpreted-model ID, carrier Product/cut, encoding profile and canonical content identity. Encoding mechanically checks J_X's subject identity/digest and retains it as evidence; D_C points to unchanged carrier identity/digest, external to it. Admitted encoding is (a_c.X.C,J_X,D_C); Product acceptance/release also point to unchanged content-first identities. Owning Products choose downstream grammar and issuance authority but cannot omit upstream IDs or substitute mutable locators.

grounding.quote:
This authoring text is a source project surface. It is neither the
identity-bearing release of this edition nor the identity-bearing source
of any released calculus edition: a dependency on a released edition
binds that edition's identity under this section, with its release,
manifest digest and member digest, and never an authoring text

constraints.statement: This edition's basis is issued only at its release under RELEASE and AC-020 after bytes exist; authoring text is neither that release nor an identity-bearing source of any released edition. Released dependencies bind edition release, manifest and member digests. Recorded predecessor coordinates are derivation provenance only: stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/, manifest 3d860ff4c1746f06ac25295a9e205cffb8e7725869615ac77cf2304b70ff2782, AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md member cbe2edb928d3e75e23446f6d525baea664966e8d5920e6fa389cbaa4af8f1f8d; stable concept identity is unchanged.
constraints.uncertainty: No issued identity for the subject edition is supplied.

grounding.quote:
This member defines the generic relations `a_c.X` and `a_c.X.C`. It
selects, constructs, accepts or releases no concrete interpretation or
carrier. A downstream authority owns its exact subject population,
interpretation, carrier, judgments and Product or release status. The
downstream identity is never embedded back into the calculus or its
publication basis

constraints.statement: Generic a_c.X/a_c.X.C relations select, construct, accept and release no concrete interpretation/carrier. Downstream authority owns exact subjects, interpretations, carriers, judgments and Product/release status. Downstream identities never enter the calculus or publication basis.

conditions: A constraint surface is used.

grounding.quote:
2. **Unresolved blocks.** A residual, a `hold`, a `gap` or an external
   predicate not yet established keeps its source and its required
   acquisition, and it blocks every operation and result that depends on
   it until its premise is established. A missing premise or an omitted
   obligation never becomes permission or a satisfied result

constraints.statement: Each element retains premise, derived consequence, policy choice, observation or unresolved-claim standing; policies retain owners and preferences do not become obligations. Construction/assurance elements retain their recorded support kind: stated formulas are not discharged and external assessments retain source/scope/evidence. Residuals, hold, gap and unestablished external predicates keep source and required acquisition and block every dependent operation/result until the premise is established. Missing premises and omitted obligations grant neither permission nor satisfaction.

conditions: A constraint surface is used.
exceptions: An approximate surface must declare its adequacy relation and end-to-end bound.

grounding.quote:
6. **Separate claims.** Structural validity of a surface is a structural
